name: Connecticut
permitAge: 16 (handbook p. 5); 18 and older get an adult learner's permit

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours behind-the-wheel training for 16- and 17-year-olds (any mix of school and home training), plus 30 hours of classroom study that includes the 8-hour safe driving course and 2-hour parent class (handbook pp. 6-7)
teen.holdPermit: 120 days after commercial or high school driver education; 180 days otherwise, including home training (handbook p. 6). Age 18+: 90 days (p. 7)
teen.nightLimit: Licensed 16 and 17: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. except employment, school, religious activities, medical necessity or Safe Ride Program (handbook p. 8). Permit: no curfew, but a qualified trainer must be in the car (DMV teen restrictions page).
teen.passengerLimit: Permit (16-17): only a licensed instructor and those with that instructor, or one qualified trainer (20+, licensed 4 consecutive years, no suspension); parents may come along (handbook p. 6). Licensed 16-17: first 6 months only instructor, parents/guardian, or one qualified trainer; months 7-12 immediate family also (handbook p. 8).
teen.phone: Under 18 (permit and licensed): no cell phone or mobile electronic device at all, hands-free included (handbook pp. 8, 11). All drivers: no hand-held device, even when stopped in traffic (p. 11). Fines $200 / $375 / $625 since Oct 2021 (housedems.ct.gov; not in handbook).

notes: Handbook: Connecticut Driver's Manual, revised March 2023 (PDF created 2023-06-02), English and Spanish PDFs on the DMV manuals page. Printed page = PDF page - 2.

Knowledge test: 25 questions, 20 correct to pass (handbook p. 5; DMV take-knowledge-vision-test page). Offered in Albanian, Arabic, Mandarin Chinese, English, French, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Vietnamese; a paper test can be requested in more languages, including Chinese Simplified and Haitian Creole (DMV page, read 2026-10-09).
Since January 1, 2026 every learner's permit applicant must first complete the free online Connecticut Work Zone Safety Course (DMV page); not in the 2023 handbook.
Failed knowledge test: wait seven days and pay $40 to retest (DMV page).
Permit valid until a license is issued or 2 years (handbook p. 5). Everyone without a prior license takes an 8-hour Safe Driving Practices course (p. 4).
Under 18 at the knowledge test: parent or guardian comes along or the applicant brings a Certificate of Parental Consent (form 2-D) (DMV teen-drivers-license page).
Move over (handbook p. 14): for any vehicle pulled over on a road, slow below the posted limit and move over one lane when safe.
Right on red after a full stop unless a sign forbids it (handbook pp. 13, 43).

Under 21: 0.02 percent zero tolerance (handbook p. 31). 48-hour license seizure for certain violations by 16-17-year-olds, vehicle may be removed (DMV teen brochure, 2020); the handbook does not mention it.
